title: Reduced Foodborne Illness Surveillance Sparks Concern About Deadlier Outbreaks
text:
Public health officials warn that recent cuts to the FoodNet surveillance system make it harder to detect and stop foodborne illness outbreaks, potentially leading to more widespread and deadly infections. Under President Donald Trump's administration, reduced funding and monitoring for pathogens like salmonella and coli raise alarms among food safety advocates.

Food safety inspections of manufacturers by the FDA plummeted from 10,641 facilities in 2011 to about 4,500 a decade later.
